simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS on success, error code otherwise

briefdescription.para: Turn a power rail on/off or switch it to a given mode.

para.verbatim: Validates the mode and requested state, applies the rail's mode transition through its PMBus or GPIO control type, waits for the supply to come up for known rails when powering on, and records the new power state.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the power rail to control
Target power state (XPM_POWER_STATE_ON or _OFF)
Mode number to transition the rail to

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS on success, error code otherwise

briefdescription.para: This routine is invoked periodically by the task scheduler and its task is to determine if a voltage adjustment is needed, based on current temperature and current voltage level.

detaileddescription.para: The argument passed points to power rail that needs to be adjusted.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the power rail (XPm_Rail) to be adjusted

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS on success, error code otherwise

briefdescription.para: Pure helper that resolves the VID source (RTCA override or eFuse cache) and computes the Performance[] Index that XPmRail_AdjustVID should switch the rail to.

para.verbatim: Side-effect-free so the decision can be invoked redundantly without re-running the rail transition. Callers should invoke this via the XPmRail_ComputeAdjustVIDIndex wrapper, which performs redundant double-call comparison on both Status and the returned Index.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the rail's VIDAdj record (RailId, Performance table, VID status).
Out: matching Performance[] entry index, or < 0 if no adjustment is required (no override, override disabled, eFuse 0, or no matching entry).

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS once *Index is set; error code on failure.

briefdescription.para: Resolve and redundantly verify a rail's VID performance index.

para.verbatim: Calls XPmRail_ComputeAdjustVIDIndexRaw() twice. Each call reads the runtime VID override and, when no override is present, the eFuse cache VID register. The two calls use separate volatile outputs; this function publishes the index only when both statuses and index values agree.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the rail's VID adjustment record containing its performance thresholds.
Output pointer receiving the agreed performance-table index, including -1 when no adjustment is required. Set only on XST_SUCCESS.

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS when both calculations succeed and agree, or XST_GLITCH_ERROR if either calculation fails or the indices differ.

briefdescription.para: Adjust a rail's voltage to the speed-grade-appropriate performance mode by transitioning it through XPmRail_Control() to the matching Performance[] entry.

para.verbatim: Reads the VID source (RTCA override or eFuse cache) via the redundant XPmRail_ComputeAdjustVIDIndex() helper, then issues a redundant XPmRail_Control() to switch the rail. On success the chosen mode is saved in PowerState and VIDAdjusted is set, which also latches the rail so a later call does nothing. PowerState is written only on that success path; InitVID already left it INVALID for every other case.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the rail to adjust. A NULL VIDAdj record means no voltage adjustment is required.

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS on success or when no adjustment is required; XST_GLITCH_ERROR if either VID calculation fails or their indices differ; or XST_FAILURE if the redundant rail transitions do not both succeed.

briefdescription.para: Return the rail mode VID picked.

para.verbatim: Only XST_SUCCESS means the rail was adjusted and the power state is good. XPM_NO_VID_ADJUST means VID left this rail alone, so the caller should use the rail default. That covers a rail with no VID record, a part with no VID in eFuse, VID switched off through the RTCA override, and an eFuse value that matched no performance entry. PowerState is written only on success; the client defaults it to XPM_VID_POWER_STATE_INVALID for all other cases.

parameterdescription.para: Power-rail node id.
Out: rail mode VID picked.

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS when the rail was adjusted; XPM_NO_VID_ADJUST when VID left it alone; XST_INVALID_PARAM on bad arguments.

briefdescription.para: Fill the persistent VID_Rails[] slot for the rail identified by Args[].

para.verbatim: Wrapped as a small static helper so it can be invoked through XSECURE_REDUNDANT_CALL and the destructive table write is hardened against single-fault skip.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the VID_Rails[] slot to populate.
CDO argument vector for XPmRail_InitVID().
Number of Performance[] entries to copy from Args[].

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS on success; XST_GLITCH_ERROR if the loop terminated early (per SW-BP-LOOP-REDUNDANCY post-loop counter check).

briefdescription.para: Initialize the VID adjustment data for a power rail.

para.verbatim: Validates the CDO argument count, rail ID and VID rail type. For a matching VID-qualified speed grade, it copies the supplied performance thresholds into a persistent table through a redundant helper call and attaches the selected table entry to the rail. Non-VID-qualified or nonmatching speed grades require no update.

parameterdescription.para: CDO arguments containing rail ID, rail type, entry count, speed-grade selector, and performance thresholds.
Number of words available in Args.

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS when the table is attached or no update applies; XST_INVALID_PARAM for malformed arguments, an unknown rail, or an invalid rail type; XST_FAILURE if either redundant table-population call fails.
